THE PROJECT FOLIO

Selected work.

Personal projects
& training

01 / Neighborhood-market demo

Store Shoppers

A local market, from basket to order.

What I builtStorefront, inventory tools, and order workflow.

Store Shoppers is a neighborhood-market demo built with Go, HTMX and SQLite. A searchable catalog leads to a basket and simulated checkout; a manager workspace handles inventory adjustments and an order queue.

Keeping the order and the shelves in sync

One Go server renders HTML, with HTMX updating forms and page fragments. Checkout saves the order and deducts stock in one SQLite transaction. Repeat submissions return the existing order; inventory adjustments keep an audit trail, and fulfillment changes follow guarded transitions.

Go · HTMX · SQLite
GitHub Live demo
02

Client + API application

A client, an API, and the transfer flow between them.

Java · Spring Boot · PostgreSQL

TEnmo uses a command-line client and a REST API to let users send, request, and approve money transfers. The backend uses Spring Data JPA and Spring Security, with PostgreSQL for data storage.

What I worked on

I worked on API request exchanges, server-side architecture, and the client-side connection logic that joins the flow together.

Across the client-server boundary

The command-line interface is the user’s entry point. Requests cross into the REST API, with PostgreSQL behind the application’s data.

03

Command-line application

Inventory, program state, and the details of a transaction.

Java · OOP · File I/O

Vendo-Matic 800 models a vending machine in a command-line application. It reads inventory from a text file and writes transactions to a log. The flow runs from a deposit and product selection through to change.

What I worked on

I worked on program-state design and refactored complex functions into smaller methods, making the transaction flow easier to follow.

From inventory to a transaction log

The inventory enters through a text file; transactions are written to a log. Between those file operations, the program handles the deposit, product selection, and change. The refactoring work focused on breaking larger functions into smaller methods around that flow.

A PERSONAL EXPERIMENT

Aethel

Public prototype · Structured writing

A structured-writing experiment built with SvelteKit, TypeScript and TipTap/ProseMirror. Explores object-reference chips, timeline state, undo/redo, browser persistence, and JSON import/export.

[[character]]→Linked object→Project file

Conceptual reference flow

References inside the text

A custom TipTap extension turns a double-bracket reference into an inline chip. It stores the object’s identifier separately from the displayed text, along with its status and color. Clicking a resolved chip can open the referenced object.

Reference extension source

Reversible changes

The editor’s history system supports undo and redo. Related operations can be grouped into one history entry; undo runs the group in reverse, and redo reapplies it in order.

Undo/redo source

A project you can save

The serialization layer gathers objects, timeline placements and timeslots, milestones, and interface state into a project file. Browser import and export use JSON, including the .aethel file extension. Import checks the expected project structure before restoring it.

Project serialization source

Background & learning
